title: CoinRun PPO one-factor bug screen
question: Which individual CR-PPO-0001 recipe difference, if any, reproduces its early policy-quality collapse when reverted alone from the validated CR-PPO-0002 recipe?
reason: CR-PPO-0002 recovered 8.671875 mean return at 25.17M steps, but it changed several settings together. Calling every difference a bug would exceed the evidence, so causal one-factor controls are required before naming a faulty training choice.
hypothesis: At least one individual reversion among 500 training levels, reward-normalizer gamma 0.999, whole-batch advantage normalization or orthogonal-sqrt2 backbone initialization will reduce the 6,291,456-step final-256 mean return by at least 1.0 or success rate by at least 0.10 versus the same-run reference repeat.
falsification: Reject the single-factor hypothesis if every reverted arm remains within 1.0 mean return and 0.10 success rate of the reference repeat; that outcome points to interactions, later-training effects or seed variance rather than one independently dominant setting.

data.training_environment: Arm-specific num_levels is the controlled variable only for levels500; all other arms use levels [0,200).

compute.estimated_budget: Five serial arms x 6,291,456 transitions = 31,457,280 transitions, expected roughly 70-100 minutes on the existing A10.
compute.shutdown_policy: Reuse the existing bounded instance timer; do not create an instance or change GPU specification.

success_criteria.rule: All five fresh arms complete exactly 6,291,456 transitions with identical evaluation identity and no checkpoint reuse.
The same-run reference repeat is evaluated on 128 periodic and 256 final episodes before any reverted arm is interpreted.
An individual factor is called independently dominant only if its final-256 mean return drops at least 1.0 or success rate drops at least 0.10 versus reference.
No trajectory collection, behavior cloning or dynamics training starts.
